chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

the one in Ihram who has intercourse with his wife: He (peace be upon him) said: If he has fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and Hajj the following year; and if he has not fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and there is not upon him Hajj the following year.

He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him; and if he was not ignorant, then upon him is the driving of a camel, and upon him is Hajj the following year.

So when he reaches the place where he had intercourse with her, their two caravans are separated, so they do not gather in one tent unless there is someone else with them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its place.

key_terms.أَفْضَى إِلَيْهَا: He fully entered into her (consummated the act)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَقَعُ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ: He has intercourse with his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiations (kaffarah) for sexual intercourse during Hajj Ihram, distinguishing liability based on full penetration versus partial contact and the state of ignorance (jahil) versus knowledge. It further elaborates on the practical ritual of separating the sacrificial animal from the pilgrim's baggage until it reaches its designated slaughter site, reflecting the juristic precision of the Imams in regulating the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.
